claims.text: The Cr-free Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has a single-phase BCC structure.
The Cr-free alloy exhibits asymmetric XRD peaks.
The asymmetric XRD peaks arise from compositional micro-segregation between dendritic and interdendritic regions.
The Cr-free alloy has low room-temperature fracture strain.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces precipitation of a complex multicomponent Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase occupies approximately 4 vol% of the alloy.
The secondary Laves phase has a C14 or C15 structure.
The Laves phase forms a reticulated, interconnected network.
The interconnected Laves phase is concentrated at grain boundaries and in interdendritic regions.
The interconnected Laves morphology forces cracks to follow tortuous paths.
Crack deflection and branching caused by the Laves network increase fracture surface area and impede crack extension.
Cr solute causes contraction of the BCC matrix lattice parameter relative to the Cr-free alloy.
Cr is smaller than the average atomic radius of the matrix constituents, making a negative lattice-parameter shift plausible.
Cr-induced lattice contraction increases the Peierls stress.
The increased Peierls stress contributes to solid-solution hardening and increased yield strength.
The interconnected Laves phase also acts as a continuous brittle pathway for crack initiation and propagation.
Embrittlement from the continuous Laves network overrides the hardening benefit and keeps room-temperature fracture strain low.
The Cr-containing alloy will have a room-temperature fracture strain below 5% despite increased yield strength.
XRD will show broadening and peak splitting associated with formation of the Laves phase.
If the BCC lattice parameter expands or does not measurably shift after Cr addition, the proposed contraction-based solid-solution-hardening mechanism is invalid.
